thread:
jen: Quick proposal  I'd like to change every public-facing occurrence of 'APAC' to 'Asia-Pacific' to reduce ambiguity in residency docs. Planning: text-only change, keep programmatic fields (region codes/endpoints) unchanged.

oliver: +1. Where should we prioritize? region matrix, endpoint pages, SDK quickstarts?

jen: start with `docs/reference/region-matrix.md`, `docs/reference/endpoints.md`, and all snippets under `docs/sdk/` and `docs/quickstarts/`. Also update the downloadable CSV header comment.

maya: small checklist from i18n perspective: 1) use "Asia-Pacific (APAC)" in table headers for tight layouts, 2) add `i18n: true` frontmatter for pages we touch, 3) avoid non-breakable space issues in translations.

ryan: note on CI: our csv shape tests check column count and code patterns. Labels are not validated, but I'll add a safeguard in the docs CI to ensure no programmatic consumers assume label tokens. Can we add a comment at top of `region-matrix.csv` like `# label: human readable only`?

jen: yes, include `# Human-facing labels only; do not rely on them for programmatic routing` at the top.

oliver: for SDK snippets: leave `region` param values as canonical codes (e.g., `ap-southeast-1`). I'll run a grep and submit a tiny PR for replacements where the comment or placeholder reads `APAC`. Command I'm using: `git grep -n "\bAPAC\b" docs | sed -n '1,200p'`.

maya: legal: @legal do we need any compliance caveats when we swap to the expanded label? Particularly around sentences that say "APAC residency" today.

legal: quick read  prefer phrasing: "Asia-Pacific (APAC)  data may be stored in Singapore, Tokyo, or Hong Kong depending on routing and configuration." Avoid implying all data is stored in one country. Also prefer using en dash for ranges.

jen: thanks. I'll adopt that exact wording in residency callouts.

ryan: search/synonym note: I'll add an Algolia synonym so searches for "APAC" still surface "Asia-Pacific" pages. Point me to the final label and I'll add it.

jen: final label for pages: `Asia-Pacific (APAC)`; for inline explanatory copy use: `Asia-Pacific  data may be stored in Singapore, Tokyo, or Hong Kong depending on routing.`

oliver: PR plan: two small PRs. One for copy updates in docs and CSV header; another for snippet changes (`i18n: true` frontmatter + comment fixes). Will link both to a Linear ticket.

docs-bot: PR 731 created by oliver: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/731  Preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood-docs.net/731

maya: once PRs land, I'll queue the strings for translation. Please set `i18n: true` in frontmatter as mentioned.

oliver: PR 731 updated per legal feedback. Replaced "APAC residency" with "Asia-Pacific (APAC)  data may be stored in Singapore, Tokyo, or Hong Kong depending on routing." Also added CSV top comment.

jen: quick reminder for docs writers: when space is constrained (mobile), use `Asia-Pacific (APAC)` in the header but elsewhere prefer the expanded form.

docs-bot: PR 732 created by oliver for SDK snippet fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/732  Preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood-docs.net/732

ryan: I added a CI check that ensures `region-matrix.csv` has a comment line starting with `# Human-facing labels` and that code columns match pattern `^[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-\d+$`. Tests passed on PRs.

legal: approved the updated residency language. Confirmed no additional compliance triggers.

maya: queued translations for merged pages. Also note: translators asked we avoid zero-width spaces in the label so locale extraction tools don't break.

oliver: merged PR 731 and PR 732.

docs-bot: PR 731 merged at 2142612620 by oliver. PR 732 merged at 2142612660 by oliver.

ryan: pushed Algolia synonym `APAC -> Asia-Pacific` and added a redirect for old `/tags/apac` to `/tags/asia-pacific`.

jen: added Linear ticket INF-1077 to track post-deploy monitoring and CS FAQ updates.

maya: leaving a note for localization: confirm character limits on mobile header before next release.

oliver: visual diffs look good. Closing this thread; reopen if anyone finds remaining `APAC` tokens.
